parties: LEAP India Limited (issuer), Book-running lead managers: JM Financial Limited, Avendus Capital Private Limited, IIFL Capital Services Limited, UBS Securities India Private Limited, Promoters: Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd. (KKR-backed) and KIA EBT Scheme 3
headline: LEAP India ₹2,480 crore mainboard IPO listed on NSE and BSE with 8.38x overall subscription
sum: KKR-backed LEAP India, India's largest on-demand asset pooling provider in supply chain management, completed its ₹2,480 crore IPO comprising ₹480 crore fresh issue and ₹2,000 crore OFS by Vertical Holdings II. The offering was oversubscribed 8.38 times (QIBs 16.84x, NIIs 12.64x, retail 1.71x) and listed on NSE at ₹165.90 and BSE at ₹166 on 14 August 2026, delivering 4.3% listing gain.
implication: Large OFS component (81% of issue) by PE-backed promoter in a capital-intensive, scale-dependent asset pooling business; valuation (~110x FY26 earnings) and restricted covenants on ₹1,018 cr borrowings require careful post-listing debt management and covenant monitoring by counsel.
detail: LEAP India, incorporated 2013, operates a share-and-reuse model for pallets, containers and material-handling equipment across 29 fulfilment centres and 10,100+ customer touchpoints serving 1,000+ customers. FY26 net profit grew 66% to ₹62.3 cr on 57% revenue growth to ₹730 cr. The fresh issue proceeds (net ~₹360 cr) are earmarked for debt repayment (~₹360 cr) and general corporate purposes. IPO price band ₹151–₹159 per share (final ₹159); anchor allocation raised ₹743.62 cr from 32 institutions on 6 August.

structure.consideration: ₹2,480 cr aggregate (₹480 cr fresh issue at ₹159/share, ₹2,000 cr OFS at ₹159/share); fresh issue 3.02 cr shares, OFS 12.58 cr shares (total 15.60 cr shares)
conditions: Anchor investor allocation: 32 institutions, ₹743.62 cr on 6 Aug at ₹159/share
QIB/NII/Retail/EMP allocation: 50% / 15% / 35% / 0.05% of net offer (15.59 cr shares)
Subscription open: 7–11 Aug 2026 (5 days, extended post-anchor)
Allotment basis: 12 Aug 2026 (computerised lottery for oversubscribed retail segment)
approvals: Conversion to public limited company: Board (27 June 2025) & shareholder special resolution (17 July 2025)
RoC certificate of incorporation (public status): 31 July 2025
RHP filed with SEBI, BSE, NSE: ~6–7 Aug 2026 (before bidding)
DRHP filed: 29 August 2025 (prior draft); SEBI clearance (formal) issued December 2025

CCI approval (presumed): implied by no regulatory delays; asset pooling/logistics not explicitly CCI-gated but market dominance (90% pallet share) suggests post-IPO CCI monitoring for abuse of dominance risk
structure.novel: Large-scale OFS (81% of issue size) by single PE sponsor (Vertical Holdings II, KKR) in a capital-intensive asset pooling platform; reflects full or partial exit by KKR post 2023 majority acquisition. Rare for Indian logistics IPO: technology-enabled asset lifecycle management (RFID, IoT, MyLEAP platform) and pan-India fulfilment network model (29 centres, 10,100+ touchpoints) pitched as differentiated from traditional 3PL. Valuation at ~110x FY26 P/E at IPO price materially above peer comparables; suggested risk of price correction post-listing (confirmed: day-1 listing 4.3%, day-1 close later -8.8%).

triggers.note: OFS mechanics: seller (Vertical Holdings II, KIA EBT) receives sale proceeds directly (not company); SEBI mandates seller lock-in exemption post-listing, triggering secondary market supply risk if promoter exits rapidly
Post-listing: quarterly earnings, material events, related-party transactions, insider trading disclosure. Company must file XBRL financials, hold audit committee meetings per board committee rules

₹1,018 cr outstanding borrowings (as of 31 Mar 2026) carry restrictive covenants (debt-to-equity, interest coverage ratios typical in asset-backed lending); IPO proceeds allocation to debt repayment (~₹360 cr) is condition precedent for covenant compliance and avoidance of cross-default

Anchor FPIs (e.g., Smallcap World Fund, Government Pension Fund Global per anchor list) trigger Schedule 4, Finance Act 1961, s. 115(2)(vii) dividend distribution tax and TDS monitoring on subsequent dividend distributions

triggers.law: Competition Act, 2002, s. 26 (CCI investigation trigger post-IPO)
triggers.note: LEAP's claimed ~90% pallet pooling market share and expansion may trigger CCI scrutiny for abuse of dominance (s. 4), predatory pricing, refusal to supply or exclusive dealing if customer complaints arise post-listing
